strengths: Addresses a genuine gap in the efficient-coding literature: existing models of energy-constrained neural codes use analytically convenient but biophysically unrealistic constraints (e.g., mean/max firing rate) that fail to explain the tuning-curve flattening with firing-rate homeostasis reported in Padamsey et al. (2022).

Elegant and rigorous unification: the proposed energy constraint (parameterized by α) and approximate homeostasis constraint are shown analytically to reduce to the constraints used in Ganguli & Simoncelli (α=1) and Wang et al. (α=3/2), providing a principled generalization rather than an ad hoc new model.

Biophysical grounding is a distinctive strength: a NEURON single-compartment simulation varying resting potential, leak conductance, and synaptic conductance is used to derive a concrete, testable dispersed-Poisson noise model and to empirically fix the exponent α=1 for real neurons, connecting abstract coding theory to measurable cellular quantities.

The derivations (Fisher information approximation, tiling reduction, homeostasis constraint, Lagrangian solutions for infomax/discrimax/Lp objectives) are worked out in detail and cross-checked in extensive appendices, including a formal proof that approximate homeostasis is an implicit property of optimality in the Ganguli & Simoncelli framework.

The paper directly compares its predictions against two existing frameworks on the same empirical benchmark and shows only the proposed model captures flattening with homeostasis simultaneously, while the alternatives predict shortening or widening with substantial homeostasis violations.
Makes concrete, falsifiable predictions (specific vrest–gleak relationships along optimal decay paths) for future patch-clamp experiments, increasing scientific value beyond curve-fitting.
weaknesses: The central empirical validation in Sec. 5 relies on fitting two free parameters (a1, a2) to match exactly two summary statistics reported in a single paper (32% widening and 29% ATP reduction), which is less a predictive test than a constrained interpolation; with two free parameters and two targets, a good fit is close to guaranteed and does not strongly discriminate the model from alternative functional forms.

Empirical grounding rests entirely on one dataset/paper (Padamsey et al. 2022); there is no validation against independent electrophysiological recordings, other species/brain areas, or the promised future patch-clamp confirmation of the predicted vrest-gleak relationships, leaving the biophysical predictions untested.

The biophysical simulation uses a single-compartment model with several simplifying choices (e.g., summarizing all leak currents into one channel, degree-8 polynomial fits for ηκ, degree up to 4 polynomial fits for κ-dependence) that appear somewhat ad hoc and risk overfitting, and whose reliability is explicitly noted to degrade outside a limited κ range (κ>130).

The approximate homeostasis constraint and the tiling approximation are only exact in special cases (uniform prior, infomax); under more realistic non-uniform priors or other objectives, homeostasis is only approximately satisfied (small but nonzero mean-FR deviations), which somewhat undercuts the paper's central claimed advantage over prior non-homeostatic models.

The mathematical framework and biophysical simulation are two fairly separable contributions loosely connected only through fitting the (a1, a2, b1, b2, η0) functions; the connection feels more like curve-fitting glue than a tight theoretical derivation linking ATP biophysics to the Fisher-information optimization.

Presentation is dense and heavily notation-laden, which may limit accessibility and reproducibility for readers outside the specific FI-based optimal-coding subfield; some key derivation steps (e.g., choice of α being fixed to exactly 1 from an affine fit) rely on empirical curve properties observed in simulation rather than derived from first principles.

The comparison to alternative models (Ganguli & Simoncelli, Wang et al.) in Fig. 4 appears to use somewhat artificial matching procedures (e.g., manually reducing R to match tuning curve peak) that may not represent the most charitable version of those models' predictions.

strengths: Addresses a genuine gap in the efficient coding literature: existing FI-based population coding models with simple energy constraints (mean/max firing rate) cannot simultaneously capture firing-rate homeostasis and tuning-curve flattening observed empirically under metabolic stress.

The paper provides a clean and elegant unification: by varying the exponent α in the generalized energy constraint (eq. 7), the framework analytically reduces to the mean-firing-rate/population-size constraint of Ganguli & Simoncelli (α=1) and the coding-capacity constraint of Wang et al. (α=3/2), situating prior models as special cases.

Grounding key parameters (α, the dispersion function η_κ(E)) in a biophysical NEURON simulation tied to ATP consumption from synaptic, spiking, and leak currents is a genuinely novel and appealing way to connect abstract information-theoretic constraints to measurable cellular quantities (resting potential, leak conductance).

Full analytical derivations (infomax, discrimax, general Lp objectives) are provided with reasonably rigorous appendices, and the approximate homeostasis constraint is shown to be an emergent property of optimality in Ganguli & Simoncelli's framework (App. E), which is a nice theoretical observation.

The qualitative structural result -- that a joint gain+density energy constraint with homeostasis naturally produces simultaneous width and amplitude changes ("flattening") rather than pure widening or pure shortening -- is a meaningful conceptual insight that follows from the model structure rather than curve-fitting alone.
weaknesses: The central empirical validation in Sec. 5 is not an independent prediction: the parameters a1, a2 of the energy budget E(κ) are explicitly fit to simultaneously reproduce the reported 32% widening and 29% ATP reduction from a single paper [22]. This is closer to calibration/curve-fitting with two free parameters matching two numbers than to a genuine out-of-sample test, which undermines the strong claims ("uniquely predicts," "accurately predicts") made about matching data.

The entire empirical grounding rests on one dataset from one study (Padamsey et al. 2022) on mouse visual cortex L2/3 neurons under long-term food restriction. No independent replication, held-out condition, or cross-validation is presented; robustness of the quantitative match to other cell types, brain regions, or metabolic stress paradigms is untested.

The comparison to Ganguli & Simoncelli and Wang et al. in Fig. 4c-d is somewhat asymmetric: those models are evaluated under constraints/priors that were not calibrated the same way the proposed model was, making the framing that only the new model achieves homeostasis feel like it favors the authors' own approach by construction rather than a fair head-to-head test.

The biophysical simulation is a highly simplified single-compartment model driven by a single deterministic input spike; spike-train level statistics are derived via an approximate analytical extrapolation with independence assumptions (App H.3) rather than direct simulation of realistic spike trains, limiting confidence in the derived noise dispersion model under naturalistic stimulus-driven firing.

Key simulation fits rely on high-order polynomials (e.g., degree 8 in v_rest/g_leak for the dispersion η_κ, degree 4 for b2(κ)), and the paper itself acknowledges these fits become unreliable outside a certain range (κ>130), raising overfitting/extrapolation concerns for a model meant to generalize.

The core mathematical machinery (FI optimization under Ganguli-Simoncelli tiling with gain/density parametrization) is an incremental extension of prior work; the primary novelty is confined to the energy constraint and its biophysical grounding, which is a narrower contribution than the framing ("a fully explainable mathematical framework that generalizes existing optimal population codes") suggests.

The approximate homeostasis constraint and tiling approximation rely on strong smoothness assumptions (p(s), g(s) smooth relative to tuning curves) and Gaussian base shapes; the paper explicitly defers extension to non-Gaussian/non-tiling populations (sigmoids, Gabors) to future work, limiting the generality of the current claims.

No experimental validation of the specific testable biophysical predictions (e.g., resting potential vs. leak conductance relationships along the optimal path) is provided; these are explicitly left to future patch-clamp experiments, meaning the paper's central biophysical claims remain unverified against direct electrophysiological measurement.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated integration of biophysical simulation (NEURON, ATP accounting) with analytical Fisher-information-based efficient coding theory, providing a mechanistic link between cellular properties and information-theoretic optimality that prior work lacked.

The proposed framework elegantly generalizes existing population coding models (Ganguli & Simoncelli; Wang et al.) as special cases (α=1, α=3/2), unifying seemingly disparate prior results under a single formalism.
Careful, extensive analytical derivations (infomax, discrimax, general Lp objectives) with detailed appendices showing self-consistency and correctness of approximations (tiling, homeostasis).

The dispersed Poisson noise model derived from simulation (variance ~ Bernoulli-like parabola scaled by ηκ) is a plausible and biophysically grounded improvement over standard Poisson noise assumptions.

The model uniquely reproduces the qualitative and, after fitting two parameters, quantitative tuning curve flattening effect reported in Padamsey et al. (2022), while alternative frameworks predict either shortening or widening, illustrating the practical relevance of the homeostasis constraint.
Generates specific, testable predictions about resting potential/leak conductance relationships across activity levels, which could be validated by future patch-clamp experiments.
Thorough documentation of simulation parameters, fitting procedures, and sensitivity analyses (e.g., effect of activity level κ, robustness of polynomial fits) supporting reproducibility.
weaknesses: The central quantitative match to data (32% widening, 29% ATP reduction) is achieved by fitting two free parameters (a1, a2) directly to these two target numbers, making the demonstration more a consistency check than an independent out-of-sample prediction; the biophysical simulation only fixes the functional form/α rather than the specific values used in the comparison.

Validation rests on a single empirical dataset (Padamsey et al., mouse V1), with quantitative agreement demonstrated for essentially one experimental condition; broader empirical support (multiple species, brain regions, or independent replication) is absent.

The comparison to alternative models (Ganguli & Simoncelli; Wang et al.) in Fig. 4 is somewhat constructed to highlight homeostasis violations under a specific configuration (uniform prior, fixed population size or fixed max firing rate); it is unclear whether more flexible parameterizations of these baselines could also approximate the data, weakening the strength of the comparative claim.

The framework relies on a chain of approximations (tiling assumption, approximate homeostasis, first-order Taylor expansions, single-compartment neuron model) whose cumulative error is not rigorously bounded beyond illustrative numerical checks, raising some concern about robustness in more general or heterogeneous population settings.
The single-compartment biophysical model is a simplification that omits dendritic and network-level energy costs, which the paper itself acknowledges as a limitation for generalizability.
The paper is dense and defers most technical substance to lengthy appendices, which may hinder accessibility and complicate independent verification of the mathematical claims within the main text.

The predicted biophysical relationships (resting potential vs. leak conductance under stress) remain untested against direct electrophysiological data in this study; the empirical validation is limited to indirect comparison of tuning curve macro-properties (width, ATP use) rather than direct fitting of individual cell parameter trajectories.

strengths: Elegant and novel theoretical unification: the paper shows that two previously disparate constraint frameworks (Ganguli & Simoncelli 2010's mean-firing-rate/population-size constraint and Wang et al. 2016a's max-firing-rate/coding-capacity constraint) are special cases (α=1, α=3/2) of a single generalized energy constraint combined with an approximate homeostasis constraint. This is a genuinely useful conceptual contribution to the population coding literature.

Biophysically grounded energy model: rather than using firing rate as an energy proxy (as essentially all prior work does), the authors build a NEURON-based single-compartment stochastic Hodgkin-Huxley simulation that accounts for synaptic, spike, and leak-current ATP costs, directly addressing a well-documented gap (Harris et al. 2012) that spikes are a minority of neuronal energy use.

Clean analytical derivations: the paper derives closed-form solutions for gain/density/Fisher information under infomax, discrimax, and general Lp objectives, with full derivations and comparisons to prior models provided in the appendix (Tables 5-7).

The model is the only one among those compared that simultaneously reproduces tuning-curve widening/flattening AND firing-rate homeostasis, whereas Ganguli & Simoncelli and Wang et al. can only match one of these phenomena at the cost of violating the other.

Extensive robustness/sensitivity analyses in the appendix: testing non-uniform priors, non-Gaussian (Gabor) tuning curves, differential noise correlations, and penalty-weight sensitivity in the relaxed optimization, all showing the qualitative flattening result is stable.

Clear and thorough related-work positioning, correctly situating the contribution among FI-based efficient coding literature and highlighting exactly which simplifying assumptions (fixed spike cost, static energy budgets) are being relaxed.
weaknesses: The core empirical validation in Section 5 is arguably circular: the two free parameters (a1, a2 in the energy-ATP mapping) are explicitly fit so that the model reproduces the exact two numbers reported by Padamsey et al. (32% widening and 29% ATP reduction) rather than being fixed a priori from simulation alone and then tested against held-out data. This weakens the claim that the model 'predicts' the empirical result rather than being calibrated to match it.

The empirical dataset used for validation (Padamsey et al. 2022) has serious limitations acknowledged by the authors themselves in Appendix M.3: the tuning curves are constructed by averaging across different cells (29 control, 32 food-restricted) rather than tracking the same cells longitudinally, undermining the statistical rigor of any quantitative fit/likelihood comparison.

The likelihood-based model comparison (Appendix M.3) reports single log-likelihood numbers without any measure of uncertainty, significance testing, or correction for differing numbers of free parameters (model selection criteria such as AIC/BIC are not used), making the 'expected ordering' claim less rigorous than it appears.

No new biological data (e.g., patch-clamp measurements of resting potential/leak conductance under metabolic stress predicted by the optimal decay path) is collected to test the model's novel, falsifiable predictions; all validation is against the single previously published dataset already used to motivate the model.

The overall framework carries substantial modeling complexity (α, β, κ, multiple fitted polynomial/rational functions for η_κ and E, tiling and homeostasis approximations) whose cumulative approximation error under realistic, non-Gaussian, non-uniform-prior conditions is only partially quantified (bounded to <0.5% deviation in select numerical experiments, but not systematically characterized).

The single-compartment biophysical simulation is a considerable simplification of real cortical neurons (no dendritic morphology, no realistic synaptic diversity, single spike input rather than naturalistic spike trains), which may limit how well the derived η_κ(E) and optimal decay paths generalize to actual cortical circuits.

It is not fully clear how α and other structural parameters would be determined prospectively for other cell types/brain areas beyond post-hoc calibration to a specific dataset, limiting the generality of the 'predictive' claims made in the abstract and discussion.

strengths: Addresses a genuine gap: existing optimal-coding frameworks (Ganguli & Simoncelli; Wang et al.) cannot jointly explain the firing-rate homeostasis and tuning-curve flattening reported by Padamsey et al. (2022), and the paper proposes a specific mechanism (energy-dependent dispersed Poisson noise with an approximate homeostasis constraint) to fill this gap.

The analytical framework is mathematically elegant and is shown rigorously to generalize prior constrained-optimization models (Ganguli & Simoncelli's mean-FR/population-size constraints, Wang et al.'s coding-capacity constraint) as special cases of a single parameterized energy constraint (Table 2, Fig. 1), which is a nice unifying contribution.

The biophysical simulation (stochastic Hodgkin-Huxley model in NEURON) grounding the noise-energy trade-off in measurable cell properties (resting potential, leak conductance) is a thoughtful attempt to connect abstract Fisher-information theory to concrete, experimentally testable biophysics, going beyond the usual simplistic 'spike rate as energy proxy' assumption.

Substantial supplementary robustness analysis (appendices) testing sensitivity to differential noise correlations, non-uniform priors, non-Gaussian (Gabor) tuning curves, and different regularization weights, showing the qualitative flattening conclusion is not fragile to these particular modeling choices.
Clear, well-organized derivations with explicit proofs connecting approximate homeostasis to known optimality conditions in prior work (Proposition E.1).
weaknesses: The central empirical validation (Section 5) rests on a single dataset (Padamsey et al. 2022) and, by the authors' own admission, that dataset averages responses across 29 vs. 32 different cells in control vs. food-restricted conditions rather than repeated measurements from the same cells—undermining the premise that spike-count variance in the data reflects a single underlying tuning curve's noise, which is exactly what the model's dispersed-Poisson machinery is meant to capture.

The quantitative match to data (32% widening, 29% ATP reduction) is achieved by fitting two free parameters (a1, a2) to satisfy essentially two target numbers, which is a calibration rather than an independent, falsifiable prediction; the paper would be far more convincing with held-out data, additional metabolic stress levels, or cross-species replication.

No new experimental or electrophysiological data are collected to test the paper's most concrete, testable predictions (specific vrest–gleak trajectories along the 'optimal path' in Fig. 3g); these are deferred entirely to 'future work,' leaving the paper's most novel biophysical claims unverified.

The single-compartment, single-spike simulation is a substantial simplification of real cortical neuron biophysics and synaptic integration (no dendritic structure, no realistic spike trains during stimulus-driven firing, only a single input spike event per trial), raising concerns about how well the derived noise-energy trade-off generalizes to realistic in vivo firing regimes.

The 'likelihood' comparison in Sec. M, intended to show the model fits data better than competitors, is computed on the same flawed cross-cell-averaged dataset and is not cross-validated or tested against alternative plausible noise models beyond the two baselines chosen, limiting how much can be concluded from the reported log-likelihood ordering.

The novelty of the core mathematical result is somewhat incremental: much of the analytical machinery (FI under tiling, gain/density decomposition, Lagrangian solution) directly reuses the Ganguli & Simoncelli / Wang et al. machinery with an added exponent α and dispersion term η_κ(E), and the 'two simple constraints' framing somewhat understates how much is inherited from prior work.

The paper's writing and presentation rely heavily on a very long appendix (36 pages of supplementary derivations/experiments) for essential robustness checks and derivations, suggesting the main text alone does not fully substantiate the claims without extensive supporting material, which may indicate the core contribution is thinner than the apparent scope suggests.

strengths: Novel and principled integration of a biophysical (NEURON, stochastic Hodgkin-Huxley) simulation with an analytical Fisher-information-based population coding framework, directly linking ATP usage to noise and tuning curve shape.

The two proposed constraints (approximate homeostasis and energy constraint) are shown analytically to generalize prior influential models (Ganguli & Simoncelli 2010; Wang et al. 2016a) as special cases (alpha=1, alpha=3/2), unifying previously disparate results in the literature.

The derived model is the only one among compared baselines that reproduces both firing-rate homeostasis and tuning curve flattening, qualitatively matching the empirical phenomenon reported in Padamsey et al. (2022), while prior models predict shortening or widening but not the combined pattern.

Extensive and careful supplementary analysis: robustness checks for non-uniform priors, non-Gaussian (Gabor) tuning curves, differential/noise correlations, and likelihood-based model comparison, all showing the core predictions are fairly robust.

Generates concrete, falsifiable predictions (resting potential vs. leak conductance relationships across activity levels) that could be tested with patch-clamp experiments, strengthening the paper's potential scientific impact.

Clear and thorough derivations (appendices) of the Fisher information approximation, dispersed Poisson noise model, and homeostasis approximation, improving reproducibility of the theoretical contributions.
weaknesses: Empirical validation rests on a single dataset (Padamsey et al. 2022) that itself has acknowledged limitations (pooled averages across 29 vs. 32 different cells rather than repeated/paired measurements from the same neurons), making the central quantitative match somewhat weak evidence.

The key quantitative match (32% widening, 29% ATP reduction) is achieved by fitting two free parameters (a1, a2) specifically to satisfy these two numbers, which is closer to curve-fitting than an independent out-of-sample prediction; no held-out or cross-validated test is provided.

The overall analytical pipeline stacks multiple approximations (tiling, homeostasis linearization, Taylor expansions, parabolic/polynomial fits to simulation outputs) without a consolidated end-to-end error analysis quantifying how these compound.

The biophysical model is a single-compartment, single-spike-input simulation; extrapolation to realistic spike trains and tuning curves relies on additional assumptions (Appendix H.3) that are not independently validated against data.
Significant modeling complexity (many fitted parameters: a1,a2,b1,b2,η0, polynomial degree choices, κ dependence) raises some overfitting/robustness concerns, even though error metrics are reported.

Model comparisons against Ganguli & Simoncelli (2010) and Wang et al. (2016a) in Fig. 4 may be somewhat construed in favor of the proposed model, since those baselines are forced to sacrifice either homeostasis or tuning width match by construction, while the new model's free parameters are tuned to satisfy both simultaneously.

The scope is restricted to scalar stimuli, Gaussian/tiling population codes, and independent (or only mildly correlated) noise; practical applicability to more realistic, multi-dimensional, or strongly correlated population codes remains untested.
